hints: Focus on what each reagent is actually testing for, oxidation needs a certain type of carbon, while sodium tests for something else.
Remember sodium metal fizzes with any compound containing an -OH group to give hydrogen gas, so look for which options have that group.
Now check which of those -OH compounds still resists oxidation because its carbon attached to OH has no hydrogen left to remove.
walkthrough:
**Understand the two tests**

Think of this as two filters. To pass, a compound must fail oxidation but pass the sodium test.

Sodium test for -OH:
$$2\text{R-OH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{R-ONa} + \text{H}_2$$

**Classify each compound**

Look at the carbon bearing the oxygen. This tells you the alcohol class.

Option A, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH}$, is a tertiary alcohol. Options C and D are primary and secondary alcohols. Option B, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, is a ketone with no -OH group.

**Apply oxidation rules**

Primary alcohols oxidise to aldehydes then acids, secondary alcohols oxidise to ketones, but tertiary alcohols cannot oxidise because there is no H on the C-OH carbon to remove.

$$\text{primary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{aldehyde} \rightarrow \text{carboxylic acid}$$
$$\text{secondary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{ketone}$$
$$\text{tertiary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{no reaction}$$

**Combine both conditions**

Only the tertiary alcohol has an -OH to react with sodium, but cannot be oxidised by acidified dichromate(VI). That is the unique match.

options.A: Correct. $(CH_3)_3COH$ is 2-methylpropan-2-ol, a tertiary alcohol. The C-OH carbon is attached to three methyl groups and has no H atom, so it cannot be oxidised by acidified $K_2Cr_2O_7$. It still contains -OH, so it reacts with Na to give $H_2$ gas and sodium tert-butoxide.
options.B: Incorrect. $CH_3COCH_2CH_3$ is butan-2-one, a ketone. Ketones indeed resist further oxidation by acidified dichromate, but with no -OH group it does not react with sodium metal. Students who only check the oxidation condition fall for this trap.
options.C: Incorrect. $CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2OH$ is butan-1-ol, a primary alcohol. It does react with sodium, but it is easily oxidised first to butanal then to butanoic acid, so it fails the 'cannot be oxidised' condition.
options.D: Incorrect. $CH_3CH_2CH(OH)CH_3$ is butan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol. It does react with sodium, but it is oxidised to the ketone butan-2-one by acidified dichromate, so it fails the 'cannot be oxidised' condition.
